source.text: Πᾶσα ψυχὴ ἐξουσίαις ὑπερεχούσαις ὑποτασσέσθω, οὐ γὰρ ἔστιν ἐξουσία εἰ μὴ ὑπὸ θεοῦ, αἱ δὲ οὖσαι ὑπὸ θεοῦ τεταγμέναι εἰσίν.

records.literal_gloss: Every soul to authorities being over [it] let be subject, not for is authority except by God, the [ones] and being by God having been appointed are.

en.L: Let every soul be subject to [the] governing authorities, for there is no authority except by God, and those that exist have been appointed by God.
en.B: Everyone must submit to the authorities who govern, because no authority exists except by God's doing, and the authorities that are in place have been put there by God.
en.R: Everyone must submit to the people who govern them. No one has authority unless God gives it. The leaders we have are there because God put them there.

es.L: Toda alma se someta a [las] autoridades que están por encima, porque no hay autoridad sino por Dios, y las que existen han sido instituidas por Dios.
es.B: Todos deben someterse a las autoridades que gobiernan, porque ninguna autoridad existe si no es por obra de Dios, y las que están en su lugar las ha puesto Dios.
es.R: Todos deben someterse a quienes los gobiernan. Nadie tiene autoridad si Dios no se la da. Los gobernantes que tenemos están ahí porque Dios los puso.

sw.L: Kila nafsi na ijitiishe chini ya mamlaka zilizo juu, kwa maana hakuna mamlaka ila kwa Mungu, na zile zilizopo zimewekwa na Mungu.
sw.B: Kila mtu anapaswa kujitiisha chini ya wenye mamlaka wanaotawala, kwa sababu hakuna mamlaka inayokuwepo isipokuwa kwa mpango wa Mungu, na wenye mamlaka waliopo wamewekwa hapo na Mungu.
sw.R: Kila mtu anapaswa kujitiisha chini ya wale wanaomtawala. Hakuna mtu mwenye mamlaka isipokuwa Mungu amempa. Viongozi tulio nao wapo kwa sababu Mungu aliwaweka hapo.

alternatives: every soul, as the inner self only
decisions.reason: "Every soul" (Πᾶσα ψυχὴ) is a Hebrew way of saying "every person", as in 2:9. It means every believer in Rome, not only the inner life.

decisions.choice: the human authorities who govern: rulers and officials of the state
alternatives: the spiritual powers thought to stand behind rulers
both human rulers and those spiritual powers
decisions.reason: ἐξουσία can be used of spiritual powers (8:38 has a related list), and some readers hear both here. But the rulers in this passage collect taxes (verses 6-7), carry the sword (verse 4) and praise good conduct (verse 3): they are the human government the readers lived under.

ὑποτασσέσθω ("be subject", literally "place oneself under") and τεταγμέναι ("appointed", "put in order") share a root with "resists" and "ordinance" in verse 2. Paul's point is that God has ordered things so, and a believer takes their place in that order.

decisions.choice: God has set up governing authority, and believers ordinarily submit to it
alternatives: every ruler and every act of a ruler has God's approval
Paul means only rulers who govern justly, as verses 3-4 describe
the command was meant only for the situation of the believers in Rome at the time
decisions.reason: Paul says no authority exists except by God, as Daniel 4:17 and John 19:11 also say. He describes what rulers are for (verses 3-4) and does not discuss here what believers should do when a ruler commands what God forbids; elsewhere the apostles say "we must obey God rather than people" (Acts 5:29), and Paul himself suffered under unjust officials (2 Corinthians 11:25). Readers have long disagreed about how far this submission reaches. The translation states only what the verse says.
Balanced and Readable say "everyone" for "every soul" (m1). "Submit" keeps the sense of placing oneself under someone, which is more than doing what one is told.

decisions.choice: No one has authority unless God gives it
alternatives: there is no authority except by God
decisions.reason: Readable turns the double negative into a plain statement with the same meaning.
"Kutii" (obey) is the everyday word, but it says only doing what one is told. "Kujitiisha chini ya" (to put oneself under) keeps the picture in the Greek verb and the play on "order" (m3).

source.text: ὥστε ὁ ἀντιτασσόμενος τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ διαταγῇ ἀνθέστηκεν, οἱ δὲ ἀνθεστηκότες ἑαυτοῖς κρίμα λήμψονται.

records.literal_gloss: So that the [one] resisting the authority the of the God ordinance has opposed, the [ones] and having opposed to themselves judgment will receive.

en.L: So then whoever resists the authority has opposed the ordinance of God, and those who have opposed [it] will receive judgment on themselves.
en.B: So anyone who sets themselves against the authority is standing against what God has ordered, and those who take that stand will bring judgment on themselves.
en.R: So anyone who fights against the authorities is fighting against what God has set up. And people who do that will be judged.

es.L: De modo que el que se opone a la autoridad se ha resistido a la ordenanza de Dios, y los que se han resistido recibirán juicio para sí mismos.
es.B: Así que quien se pone en contra de la autoridad está haciendo frente a lo que Dios ha ordenado, y los que adoptan esa postura atraerán juicio sobre sí mismos.
es.R: Por eso, quien lucha contra las autoridades está luchando contra lo que Dios estableció. Y los que hacen eso serán juzgados.

sw.L: Hivyo basi, anayeipinga mamlaka ameupinga utaratibu wa Mungu, na wale waliopinga watapokea hukumu juu yao wenyewe.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, mtu anayejiweka kinyume na mamlaka anasimama kinyume na utaratibu ambao Mungu ameuweka, na wanaosimama hivyo watajiletea hukumu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, mtu anayepigana dhidi ya wenye mamlaka anapigana dhidi ya kile ambacho Mungu amekiweka. Na watu wanaofanya hivyo watahukumiwa.

decisions.reason: ἀντιτασσόμενος ("resisting", literally "ranging oneself against") and διαταγῇ ("ordinance") carry on the play on the root "order" from verse 1: to set oneself against the order of government is to set oneself against God's arrangement.

decisions.choice: judgment, without saying who gives it
alternatives: punishment by the ruler, acting as God's servant
decisions.reason: κρίμα is a judgment against someone. Paul does not say whether it comes from God or from the ruler; verse 4 suggests the ruler carries it out as God's servant, so both may be in view. The translation leaves it open, as the Greek does.
Balanced and Readable use a phrase that shows the picture of taking a stand against someone.
Readable uses a passive, which keeps open who does the judging (m2).
"Utaratibu" is an order or arrangement, which keeps the link with the root "order" that runs through verses 1-2 (m1). "Agizo" or "amri" would make it a single command.

source.text: οἱ γὰρ ἄρχοντες οὐκ εἰσὶν φόβος τῷ ἀγαθῷ ἔργῳ ἀλλὰ τῷ κακῷ.

records.literal_gloss: The for rulers not are a terror to the good work but to the evil.

en.L: For rulers are not a terror to good work, but to evil.
en.B: Rulers are not something to fear when you do what is good, only when you do what is wrong.
en.R: People who do good do not need to be afraid of rulers. Only people who do wrong need to fear them.

es.L: Porque los gobernantes no son terror para la buena obra, sino para la mala.
es.B: Los gobernantes no son algo que temer cuando uno hace el bien, sino solo cuando hace el mal.
es.R: Quien hace el bien no tiene por qué tener miedo de los gobernantes. Solo deben temerlos los que hacen el mal.

sw.L: Kwa maana watawala si kitisho kwa kazi njema, bali kwa [kazi] mbaya.
sw.B: Watawala hawapaswi kuogopwa na mtu anayetenda mema, bali na anayetenda mabaya tu.
sw.R: Watu wanaotenda mema hawana sababu ya kuwaogopa watawala. Ni wale tu wanaotenda mabaya wanaopaswa kuwaogopa.

decisions.reason: ἔργῳ ("work") is a single deed or a way of acting. It has nothing to do with "works of the law" here; Paul contrasts doing good with doing evil.

decisions.choice: what rulers are for, stated generally
alternatives: a promise that every ruler will in fact reward good and punish evil
decisions.reason: Paul describes the purpose God gave to rulers. He knew that rulers could act unjustly: he had been beaten and imprisoned by city officials (Acts 16:22-23). The sentence says what government is meant to do, not that it always does it.

decisions.choice: when you do what is good / wrong
alternatives: a terror to good conduct, but to bad
decisions.reason: "A terror to good work" is hard to follow in English. Balanced and Readable say it from the point of view of the person doing good or wrong.

source.text: θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν;

records.literal_gloss: Want you and not to fear the authority?

en.L: And do you wish not to fear the authority?
en.B: Would you like to have no fear of the one in authority?
en.R: Do you want to live without being afraid of the people in charge?

es.L: ¿Y quieres no temer a la autoridad?
es.B: ¿Te gustaría no tener miedo de quien tiene la autoridad?
es.R: ¿Quieres vivir sin miedo a los que mandan?

sw.B: Je, ungependa kutomwogopa yeye aliye na mamlaka?
sw.R: Je, unataka kuishi bila kuwaogopa watu wanaoongoza?

decisions.reason: θέλεις is singular. Paul turns to an imagined single listener, as he often does in Romans (2:1, 2:17, 9:19), to make the point personal.

decisions.choice: the authority: the person who holds it
decisions.reason: Here "the authority" is the official who holds power, as the next sentences show.
Paul turns to a single imagined listener (m1), so verses 3-4 use "tú", which is the same in Latin America and Spain. Only the plural "you" of the letter is a reader setting.

source.text: τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει, καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς·

records.literal_gloss: The good do, and you will have praise from it;

en.L: Do what is good, and you will have praise from it;
en.B: Then do what is good, and you will receive its approval.
en.R: Then do what is right, and they will praise you.

es.L: Haz lo bueno, y tendrás alabanza de ella;
es.B: Entonces haz lo bueno, y recibirás su aprobación.
es.R: Entonces haz lo que es correcto, y te elogiarán.

sw.L: Tenda lililo jema, nawe utapata sifa kutoka kwayo;
sw.B: Basi tenda yaliyo mema, nawe utapata kibali chake.
sw.R: Basi fanya yaliyo sawa, nao watakusifu.

decisions.choice: praise: public approval and honor from those who govern
decisions.reason: ἔπαινον is praise or commendation. Greek cities publicly honored people who did good for the city, sometimes with inscriptions; Paul's readers would know that kind of praise.
αὐτῆς ("it") refers back to "the authority" in the question just before.
Readable has been speaking of "the people in charge", so it says "they".

source.text: θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν σοὶ εἰς τὸ ἀγαθόν.

records.literal_gloss: Of God for servant it is to you for the good.

en.L: For [it] is God's servant to you for the good.
en.B: For the ruler is God's servant, working for your good.
en.R: The people in charge are serving God, and they are there to help you.

es.L: Porque es servidor de Dios para ti, para el bien.
es.B: Pues el gobernante es servidor de Dios, que trabaja para tu bien.
es.R: Los que mandan están sirviendo a Dios, y están ahí para ayudarte.

sw.L: Kwa maana [mwenye mamlaka] ni mtumishi wa Mungu kwako, kwa ajili ya wema.
sw.B: Kwa maana mtawala ni mtumishi wa Mungu, anayefanya kazi kwa faida yako.
sw.R: Viongozi wanamtumikia Mungu, na wapo ili kukusaidia.

decisions.choice: servant: one who acts for another, here God's agent
decisions.reason: διάκονός is someone who acts on behalf of another. Paul uses the same word for himself and for Phoebe (16:1). Here it is a civil official doing God's work, whether or not the official knows it.

decisions.choice: the subject is the one in authority
decisions.reason: The verb ἐστιν has no stated subject. It continues from "the authority" in verse 3, now thought of as the person who holds it.

decisions.choice: [it] / the ruler / the people in charge
decisions.reason: Each level states the subject the Greek leaves understood (m2). Readable makes it plural, to match its wording in verse 3.
As elsewhere in Paul's letters, "servidor" renders this word and "esclavo" the word for a slave. "Siervo" is avoided because older Spanish Bibles use it for the slave word.
As elsewhere in Paul's letters, "mtumishi" (servant) renders this word and "mtumwa" the word for a slave.

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ τὸ κακὸν ποιῇς, φοβοῦ· οὐ γὰρ εἰκῇ τὴν μάχαιραν φορεῖ· θεοῦ γὰρ διάκονός ἐστιν, ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι.

records.literal_gloss: If but the evil you do, fear; not for in vain the sword it bears; of God for servant it is, avenger for wrath to the [one] the evil practicing.

en.L: But if you do evil, be afraid; for [it] does not bear the sword in vain; for [it] is God's servant, an avenger for wrath to the one who practices evil.
en.B: But if you do wrong, be afraid, because the ruler does not carry the sword for nothing. The ruler is God's servant, one who avenges and brings wrath on anyone who does wrong.
en.R: But if you do wrong, you should be afraid. Rulers have the power to punish, and they do not have it for nothing. They serve God, and through them God's anger comes on people who do wrong.

es.L: Pero si haces lo malo, teme; porque no en vano lleva la espada; porque es servidor de Dios, vengador para ira al que practica lo malo.
es.B: Pero si haces el mal, ten miedo, porque el gobernante no lleva la espada sin motivo. Es servidor de Dios, un vengador que trae la ira sobre quien hace el mal.
es.R: Pero si haces lo malo, debes tener miedo. Los gobernantes tienen poder para castigar, y no lo tienen por nada. Sirven a Dios, y por medio de ellos la ira de Dios cae sobre los que hacen el mal.

sw.L: Lakini kama unatenda mabaya, uwe na hofu; kwa maana si bure kwamba anabeba upanga; kwa maana ni mtumishi wa Mungu, mlipizaji kisasi kwa ajili ya ghadhabu kwa anayetenda mabaya.
sw.B: Lakini ukifanya mabaya, basi uogope, kwa sababu mtawala hashiki upanga bila sababu. Yeye ni mtumishi wa Mungu, anayelipiza kisasi na kuleta ghadhabu juu ya mtu yeyote anayefanya mabaya.
sw.R: Lakini ukifanya mabaya, unapaswa kuogopa. Watawala wana uwezo wa kuadhibu, na hawakupewa uwezo huo bure. Wanamtumikia Mungu, na kupitia wao ghadhabu ya Mungu inawajia watu wanaofanya mabaya.

decisions.choice: bearing the sword: the power to punish, up to the death penalty
alternatives: a soldier's or police officer's weapon only
decisions.reason: In the Roman world the sword (μάχαιραν) stood for a ruler's power to punish, including the power to put to death. Paul means that power, not only a weapon.

decisions.choice: God's wrath carried out through the ruler
decisions.reason: In 12:19 Paul told believers not to take revenge but to leave room for God's wrath. Here he uses the same words: the ruler is an avenger (ἔκδικος) for wrath (ὀργὴν). God's justice works through the ruler, so believers themselves need not take revenge.
εἰκῇ means without cause or to no purpose. The ruler's power to punish has a purpose.
Readable explains what bearing the sword meant (m1).

decisions.choice: through them God's anger comes on
decisions.reason: Readable says whose wrath it is (m2) and uses the simpler word "anger".

source.text: διὸ ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι, οὐ μόνον διὰ τὴν ὀργὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ διὰ τὴν συνείδησιν, διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε, λειτουργοὶ γὰρ θεοῦ εἰσιν εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο προσκαρτεροῦντες.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore [it is] necessary to be subject, not only because of the wrath but also because of the conscience, \v 6 because of this for also taxes you pay, servants for of God they are for this very [thing] attending constantly.

en.L: Therefore [it is] necessary to be subject, not only because of the wrath but also because of conscience. \v 6 For because of this you also pay taxes, for they are servants of God, devoting themselves to this very thing.
en.B: So you must submit, not only to escape wrath but also for the sake of conscience. \v 6 This is the reason you also pay taxes: those in authority serve God in a public office, and they give themselves to this very task.
en.R: So you must submit to them. Do it not only because you are afraid of being punished, but also because you know in your heart that it is right. \v 6 That is also why you pay taxes. Rulers are doing work for God when they give their time to governing.

es.L: Por tanto, [es] necesario someterse, no solo a causa de la ira, sino también a causa de la conciencia. \v 6 Porque por esto también {{plural_you:pagan|pagáis}} impuestos, pues son ministros de Dios, dedicados sin cesar a esto mismo.
es.B: Por eso hay que someterse, no solo para escapar de la ira, sino también por motivo de conciencia. \v 6 Esta es también la razón por la que {{plural_you:pagan|pagáis}} impuestos: los que gobiernan son ministros de Dios en el servicio público, y se entregan a esta misma tarea.
es.R: Por eso {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} {{plural_you:someterse|someteros}} a ellos. No lo {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} solo por miedo al castigo, sino también porque en el fondo {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} que es lo correcto. \v 6 Por eso también {{plural_you:pagan|pagáis}} impuestos. Los gobernantes trabajan para Dios cuando dedican su tiempo a gobernar.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo [ni] lazima kujitiisha, si kwa sababu ya ghadhabu tu, bali pia kwa ajili ya dhamiri. \v 6 Kwa maana ndiyo sababu pia mnatoa kodi, kwa kuwa [wao ni] watumishi wa umma wa Mungu, wakijitoa daima kwa jambo hili hili.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo ni lazima mjitiishe, si ili kuepuka ghadhabu tu, bali pia kwa ajili ya dhamiri. \v 6 Hii ndiyo sababu pia mnalipa kodi: wenye mamlaka ni watumishi wa Mungu katika kazi ya umma, nao wanajitoa kwa kazi hii hasa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mnapaswa kujitiisha chini yao. Fanyeni hivyo si tu kwa sababu mnaogopa kuadhibiwa, bali pia kwa sababu mnajua moyoni mwenu kwamba ni sawa. \v 6 Ndiyo sababu pia mnalipa kodi. Watawala wanafanya kazi ya Mungu wanapotumia muda wao kutawala.

decisions.choice: conscience: knowing before God that submitting is right
alternatives: fear of what others will think
decisions.reason: συνείδησιν is a person's inner knowledge of right and wrong. Since authorities are put in place by God (verse 1), a believer submits because it is right before God, not only out of fear of punishment ("the wrath" of verse 4).
τελεῖτε can be read as a statement or a command. The word "for" makes it a statement: Paul points to something his readers already do as evidence for what he has said. Verse 7 then gives the command.

λειτουργοὶ was used in Greek for people who served their city, often at their own cost, and in the Greek Old Testament for priests and temple servants. Paul uses it of himself in 15:16. Here it is officials in public service, who serve God even in their ordinary work.

decisions.choice: devoted to this very thing: the work of governing
decisions.reason: "This very thing" is most naturally the work just described: rewarding good, punishing wrong, and so serving God. It may also include the collecting of taxes just mentioned.

decisions.choice: afraid of being punished / you know in your heart that it is right
alternatives: because of the wrath / because of conscience
decisions.reason: Readable explains both reasons in plain words (m1).

decisions.choice: serve God in a public office
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the public side of the word (m3), which a plain "servants" loses.
As throughout the letter, every plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (default) or vosotros.
"Servidor" is kept for the word in verse 4. "Ministro" is both a public official and one who serves in worship, which is close to the two uses of this Greek word (m3).

decisions.choice: watumishi wa umma / watumishi wa Mungu katika kazi ya umma
decisions.reason: "Watumishi wa umma" is the ordinary Swahili term for public servants, which fits this word (m3) and sets it apart from plain "mtumishi" in verse 4. It loses the word's link with temple service, which the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ἀπόδοτε πᾶσι τὰς ὀφειλάς, τῷ τὸν φόρον τὸν φόρον, τῷ τὸ τέλος τὸ τέλος, τῷ τὸν φόβον τὸν φόβον, τῷ τὴν τιμὴν τὴν τιμήν.

records.literal_gloss: Give back to all the debts, to the [one] the tax the tax, to the [one] the toll the toll, to the [one] the fear the fear, to the [one] the honor the honor.

en.L: Give back to everyone what is owed: to the one [owed] tax, the tax; to the one [owed] toll, the toll; to the one [owed] fear, the fear; to the one [owed] honor, the honor.
en.B: Pay everyone what you owe them: taxes to the one who collects taxes, customs to the one who collects customs, respect to the one who is owed respect, honor to the one who is owed honor.
en.R: Give everyone what you owe them. If you owe taxes, pay your taxes. If you owe fees on goods, pay them. If someone should be respected, respect them. If someone should be honored, honor them.

es.L: {{plural_you:Devuelvan|Devolved}} a todos lo que se debe: al que [se le debe] tributo, el tributo; al que peaje, el peaje; al que temor, el temor; al que honra, la honra.
es.B: {{plural_you:Paguen|Pagad}} a cada uno lo que le {{plural_you:deben|debéis}}: impuestos a quien cobra impuestos, aranceles a quien cobra aranceles, respeto a quien se debe respeto, honra a quien se debe honra.
es.R: {{plural_you:Den|Dad}} a cada uno lo que le {{plural_you:deben|debéis}}. Si {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} impuestos, {{plural_you:paguen|pagad}} los impuestos. Si {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} derechos por mercancías, {{plural_you:páguenlos|pagadlos}}. Si alguien merece respeto, {{plural_you:respétenlo|respetadlo}}. Si alguien merece honra, {{plural_you:hónrenlo|honradlo}}.

sw.L: Rudisheni kwa wote mnachodaiwa: kwa [anayedai] kodi, kodi; kwa [anayedai] ushuru, ushuru; kwa [anayedai] hofu, hofu; kwa [anayedai] heshima, heshima.
sw.B: Mlipeni kila mtu kile mnachodaiwa naye: kodi kwa anayekusanya kodi, ushuru kwa anayekusanya ushuru, staha kwa anayestahili staha, heshima kwa anayestahili heshima.
sw.R: Mpeni kila mtu kile mnachodaiwa. Ikiwa mnadaiwa kodi, lipeni kodi. Ikiwa mnadaiwa ushuru wa bidhaa, lipeni ushuru huo. Ikiwa mtu anastahili staha, mpeni staha. Ikiwa mtu anastahili heshima, mheshimuni.

decisions.reason: φόρον was the direct tax paid by people under Roman rule, on land and persons; τέλος here means indirect taxes such as tolls and customs on goods. In this verse τέλος does not have its sense "end".

decisions.choice: fear: the respect owed to those in high office
alternatives: fear owed to God alone, with honor owed to rulers
decisions.reason: φόβον is the same word as "terror" in verse 3, now as the respect owed to those over us. Some read it as the fear owed to God, as in 1 Peter 2:17 ("fear God, honor the king"), so that the verse would end with a contrast. But the list moves from one kind of debt to the next, and nothing marks a change from rulers to God.

decisions.choice: a possible echo of Jesus' saying about paying Caesar
decisions.reason: ἀπόδοτε ("give back", "pay what is due") is the verb Jesus used: "give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God" (Mark 12:17). Paul does not quote the saying, and the echo may not be intended.
In English "fear" for a ruler suggests terror; Balanced and Readable say "respect" for the honor owed to an office (m2). Literal keeps "fear".
The English words name the indirect taxes the word meant (m1).

Swahili "heshima" covers both respect and honor, so the list would say the same word twice. Balanced and Readable use "staha" (deference, the respect owed to those over us) for the first word (m2) and "heshima" for the second. Literal keeps "hofu" (fear).

source.text: Μηδενὶ μηδὲν ὀφείλετε, εἰ μὴ τὸ ἀλλήλους ἀγαπᾶν· ὁ γὰρ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἕτερον νόμον πεπλήρωκεν.

records.literal_gloss: To no one anything owe, except the one another to love; the [one] for loving the other law has fulfilled.

en.L: Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for the one who loves the other has fulfilled [the] law.
en.B: Do not stay in debt to anyone, except for the debt of love you owe one another. Whoever loves another person has fulfilled the law.
en.R: Do not leave any debt unpaid, except one: the love you owe each other. Anyone who loves other people has done what the law requires.

es.L: No {{plural_you:deban|debáis}} nada a nadie, sino el {{plural_you:amarse|amaros}} unos a otros; porque el que ama al otro ha cumplido [la] ley.
es.B: No {{plural_you:queden|quedéis}} en deuda con nadie, salvo la deuda de amor que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} unos con otros. Quien ama a otra persona ha cumplido la ley.
es.R: No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} ninguna deuda sin pagar, excepto una: el amor que {{plural_you:se deben|os debéis}} unos a otros. El que ama a los demás ha hecho lo que la ley pide.

sw.L: Msiwe na deni la chochote kwa mtu yeyote, ila kupendana ninyi kwa ninyi; kwa kuwa anayempenda mwingine ametimiza sheria.
sw.B: Msibaki na deni kwa mtu yeyote, isipokuwa deni la upendo, ambalo mnadaiwa ninyi kwa ninyi. Mtu anayempenda mtu mwingine ametimiza sheria.
sw.R: Msiache deni lolote bila kulipa, isipokuwa moja: upendo mnaodaiwa kati yenu. Mtu anayewapenda wengine amefanya yote ambayo sheria inataka.

decisions.reason: ὀφείλετε can be a command or a statement. Following the command of verse 7, it is a command. It plays on the "debts" of verse 7: pay every debt, except the one that can never be paid off.

decisions.choice: love as a debt that always remains
decisions.reason: Believers are to clear every other debt, but love for one another is a debt they keep owing and keep paying. It is never settled.

decisions.choice: loves the other person; has fulfilled the law
alternatives: has fulfilled the other law (the law about others)
decisions.reason: "The other" (ἕτερον) is most naturally the one who is loved, the other person, as in 2:1 and 13:9's "neighbor". It could grammatically go with "law" instead, but Paul does not speak of an "other law" anywhere here.
νόμον has no article, but it is Moses' law, as the commandments quoted in verse 9 show.

decisions.choice: the debt of love you owe / the love you owe
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the picture of a debt explicit, as the Greek implies by "owe" (m1).

source.text: τὸ γάρ· Οὐ μοιχεύσεις, Οὐ φονεύσεις, Οὐ κλέψεις, Οὐκ ἐπιθυμήσεις, καὶ εἴ τις ἑτέρα ἐντολή, ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται, ἐν τῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The for: Not you shall commit adultery, Not you shall murder, Not you shall steal, Not you shall covet, and if any other commandment, in the word this it is summed up, in the: You shall love the neighbor of you as yourself.

en.L: For the [saying], "You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet," and if [there is] any other commandment, it is summed up in this word, in this: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
en.B: Take the commandments "Do not commit adultery," "Do not murder," "Do not steal," "Do not covet": these, and whatever other commandment there is, are gathered up in this one saying: "You must love your neighbor as you love yourself."
en.R: God's law says, "Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not want what belongs to someone else." All these commands, and every other one, come down to this one: "Love your neighbor as much as you love yourself."

es.L: Porque el [dicho]: «No cometerás adulterio, no asesinarás, no robarás, no codiciarás», y si [hay] algún otro mandamiento, en esta palabra se resume, en esto: «Amarás a tu prójimo como a ti mismo».
es.B: Los mandamientos «No cometas adulterio», «No asesines», «No robes», «No codicies», y cualquier otro mandamiento que haya, se resumen en esta sola palabra: «Debes amar a tu prójimo como te amas a ti mismo».
es.R: La ley de Dios dice: «No cometas adulterio. No asesines. No robes. No desees lo que es de otro». Todos estos mandamientos, y cualquier otro, se reducen a este: «Ama a tu prójimo tanto como te amas a ti mismo».

sw.L: Kwa maana lile [neno]: "Usizini, Usiue, Usiibe, Usitamani," na kama iko amri nyingine yoyote, imefupishwa katika neno hili, katika lile: "Utampenda jirani yako kama wewe mwenyewe."
sw.B: Amri hizi, "Usizini," "Usiue," "Usiibe," "Usitamani," pamoja na amri nyingine yoyote iliyopo, zote zimekusanywa katika neno hili moja: "Mpende jirani yako kama unavyojipenda mwenyewe."
sw.R: Sheria ya Mungu inasema, "Usizini. Usiue. Usiibe. Usitamani kitu cha mtu mwingine." Amri hizi zote, na nyingine zote, zinafupishwa kuwa amri hii moja: "Mpende jirani yako kama vile unavyojipenda mwenyewe."

decisions.choice: commandments from the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:13-17; Deuteronomy 5:17-21)
decisions.reason: Paul quotes four of the commandments about how to treat a neighbor. He puts adultery before murder, as Luke 18:20 and James 2:11 also do; the Hebrew text has murder first.

Paul quotes the command to love one's neighbor from Leviticus 19:18, in the words of the Greek translation of the Old Testament, as in Galatians 5:14. Jesus named it as the second great command (Mark 12:31).

decisions.choice: summed up: gathered under one head
decisions.reason: ἀνακεφαλαιοῦται is to sum up, to bring many things together under one heading. The love command does not do away with the others; it states what they all have in common.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT text, with four commandments
alternatives: some manuscripts add "you shall not bear false witness" after "you shall not steal"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, and the King James Version which follows the later Greek editions, include the commandment against false witness. The earliest manuscripts do not, and the SBLGNT leaves it out. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; to be checked against the apparatus.)
Readable names where the commandments come from (m1).

decisions.choice: want what belongs to someone else
decisions.reason: Readable explains "covet", which is not an everyday word.
Balanced and Readable word the quotation as in Galatians 5:14.
"No matarás" is the familiar wording, but the Greek verb is murder, not every kind of killing; "asesinar" says that, and it is an everyday word.

source.text: ἡ ἀγάπη τῷ πλησίον κακὸν οὐκ ἐργάζεται· πλήρωμα οὖν νόμου ἡ ἀγάπη.

records.literal_gloss: The love to the neighbor evil not works; fulfillment therefore of law the love.

en.L: Love does not work evil to the neighbor; therefore love [is the] fulfillment of [the] law.
en.B: Love does no harm to a neighbor, and so love is what fulfills the law.
en.R: People who love others do not harm them. So love does all that the law asks.

es.L: El amor no obra mal al prójimo; por tanto, el amor [es] plenitud de [la] ley.
es.B: El amor no causa daño al prójimo, y así el amor es lo que da cumplimiento a la ley.
es.R: Quien ama a los demás no les hace daño. Así, el amor hace todo lo que la ley pide.

sw.L: Upendo haumtendei jirani ubaya; kwa hiyo upendo [ni] utimilifu wa sheria.
sw.B: Upendo haumdhuru jirani, na kwa hiyo upendo ndio unaotimiza sheria.
sw.R: Watu wanaowapenda wengine hawawadhuru. Kwa hiyo upendo unafanya yote ambayo sheria inataka.

decisions.reason: The commandments of verse 9 all forbid harming a neighbor. Love fulfills them by never doing the harm they forbid; it does far more than that, but this is Paul's point here.

decisions.choice: fulfillment: what the law aims at, carried out
alternatives: only a summary of the law
decisions.reason: πλήρωμα is the full measure or the carrying out of something. When people love, what the law commands actually happens (as in Galatians 5:14).
Doing "evil" to a neighbor means harming them; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: Καὶ τοῦτο εἰδότες τὸν καιρόν, ὅτι ὥρα ἤδη ὑμᾶς ἐξ ὕπνου ἐγερθῆναι, νῦν γὰρ ἐγγύτερον ἡμῶν ἡ σωτηρία ἢ ὅτε ἐπιστεύσαμεν.

records.literal_gloss: And this knowing the time, that [it is] hour already you out of sleep to be raised, now for nearer of us the salvation than when we believed.

en.L: And [do] this, knowing the time, that [it is] already [the] hour for you to be raised out of sleep, for now our salvation [is] nearer than when we believed.
en.B: Do this because you know what time it is: it is already time for you to wake up out of sleep. Our salvation is closer now than it was when we first believed.
en.R: Do all this because you know what time it is. It is time to wake up! The day when God will save us completely is closer now than when we first believed.

es.L: Y esto, sabiendo el tiempo: que ya [es] hora de que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} levantados del sueño, porque ahora nuestra salvación [está] más cerca que cuando creímos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} esto porque {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} en qué tiempo {{plural_you:viven|vivís}}: ya es hora de que {{plural_you:despierten|despertéis}} del sueño. Nuestra salvación está ahora más cerca que cuando creímos por primera vez.
es.R: {{plural_you:Hagan|Haced}} todo esto, porque {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} qué hora es. ¡Ya es hora de despertar! El día en que Dios nos salvará por completo está más cerca ahora que cuando creímos por primera vez.

sw.L: Na [fanyeni] hili, mkijua wakati, kwamba tayari [ni] saa yenu kuinuliwa kutoka usingizini, kwa maana wokovu wetu sasa [uko] karibu zaidi kuliko wakati tulipoamini.
sw.B: Fanyeni hivyo kwa sababu mnajua ni wakati gani huu: tayari ni wakati wenu wa kuamka usingizini. Wokovu wetu uko karibu zaidi sasa kuliko wakati tulipoamini kwa mara ya kwanza.
sw.R: Fanyeni haya yote kwa sababu mnajua ni saa ngapi. Ni wakati wa kuamka! Siku ambayo Mungu atatuokoa kikamilifu iko karibu zaidi sasa kuliko tulipoamini mara ya kwanza.

decisions.choice: and do this: carry out what has just been said
decisions.reason: "And this" (Καὶ τοῦτο) has no verb. It points back to the commands of 12:1-13:10, especially love, and adds a reason to keep them: the time is short.

decisions.choice: the time: this decisive moment in God's plan
decisions.reason: καιρόν is a fitting or decisive time. Paul means the present age, close to its end, before Christ returns and God's day comes (verse 12).

decisions.choice: salvation in its completion at Christ's return
decisions.reason: σωτηρία here is still to come and is coming nearer. Paul speaks of salvation as both begun and still to be completed (5:9-10; 8:23-24); here he means its completion.

decisions.choice: waking from sleep: becoming alert and ready
decisions.reason: Sleep is a picture of carelessness about God's coming day, as in 1 Thessalonians 5:6-8.
"When we believed" means when we came to faith; "first" makes that clear.

decisions.choice: the day when God will save us completely
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of salvation is meant (m3).

source.text: ἡ νὺξ προέκοψεν, ἡ δὲ ἡμέρα ἤγγικεν.

records.literal_gloss: The night has advanced, the and day has drawn near.

en.L: The night has advanced, and the day has drawn near.
en.B: The night is almost over; the day is close.
en.R: The night is nearly over. Soon it will be day.

es.L: La noche ha avanzado, y el día se ha acercado.
es.B: La noche ya casi termina; el día está cerca.
es.R: La noche casi ha terminado. Pronto será de día.

sw.L: Usiku umesonga mbele, na mchana umekaribia.
sw.B: Usiku unakaribia kwisha; mchana u karibu.

decisions.choice: night: the present age; day: the coming day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Paul uses night and day for the present age and the day of Christ's coming, as in 1 Thessalonians 5:2-8. The picture of dawn carries on from "wake up" in verse 11.

decisions.choice: the night far gone, the day already near
decisions.reason: προέκοψεν is to advance or go forward: the night is well on its way to ending. ἤγγικεν (perfect) means the day has come near and is now close.

Swahili has "siku" for a day (and for the Day of the Lord) and "mchana" for daylight. Paul's picture is of night giving way to daylight, so Swahili says "mchana" here and in verse 13; the meaning decision (m1) explains that the coming day of the Lord is meant.

source.text: ἀποβαλώμεθα οὖν τὰ ἔργα τοῦ σκότους, ἐνδυσώμεθα δὲ τὰ ὅπλα τοῦ φωτός.

records.literal_gloss: Let us throw off therefore the works of the darkness, let us put on and the weapons of the light.

en.L: Therefore let us throw off the works of darkness, and let us put on the weapons of light.
en.B: So let us take off the deeds that belong to darkness and put on the armor of light.
en.R: So let us get rid of the evil things that belong to the dark. Let us put on light as our armor.

es.L: Así que despojémonos de las obras de la oscuridad y revistámonos de las armas de la luz.
es.B: Así que quitémonos las acciones que pertenecen a la oscuridad y vistámonos con la armadura de la luz.
es.R: Así que dejemos las cosas malas que son propias de la oscuridad. Pongámonos la luz como armadura.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo tuyatupilie mbali matendo ya giza, na tuvae silaha za nuru.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo tuvue kama nguo matendo yaliyo ya giza, na tuvae deraya ya nuru.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo tuache mambo mabaya yanayofanywa gizani. Tuvae nuru kama vazi la vita.

decisions.reason: ἔργα here are deeds, the evil things people do at night or in hiding (verse 13 lists them). It has nothing to do with "works of the law".
ὅπλα covers both weapons and armor (6:13 uses it of the body's parts as tools or weapons). With "put on", the picture is of armor, as in 1 Thessalonians 5:8.

decisions.choice: taking off and putting on: a change in how one lives
decisions.reason: Taking off and putting on clothes is a common biblical picture of leaving one way of life and taking up another (Colossians 3:8-12). Verse 14 carries it on.
Balanced and Readable say "deeds" or "evil things" for these actions (m1); Literal keeps "works".
Balanced and Readable follow the clothing picture (m2); Literal keeps "weapons".
"Silaha" means weapons only. With "put on" the picture is armor (m2), so Balanced says "deraya" (armor) and Readable "vazi la vita" (battle clothing). Literal keeps "silaha".

source.text: ὡς ἐν ἡμέρᾳ εὐσχημόνως περιπατήσωμεν, μὴ κώμοις καὶ μέθαις, μὴ κοίταις καὶ ἀσελγείαις, μὴ ἔριδι καὶ ζήλῳ, ἀλλὰ ἐνδύσασθε τὸν κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, καὶ τῆς σαρκὸς πρόνοιαν μὴ ποιεῖσθε εἰς ἐπιθυμίας.

records.literal_gloss: As in day properly let us walk, not in revelries and drunkenness, not in beds and sensuality, not in strife and jealousy, \v 14 but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and of the flesh provision not make for desires.

en.L: Let us walk properly, as in [the] day, not in revelries and drunkenness, not in sexual promiscuity and debauchery, not in strife and jealousy; \v 14 but put on the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, and make no provision for the flesh, for [its] desires.
en.B: Let us live decently, as people do in the daytime: not in wild parties and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and shameless excess, not in quarrels and envy. \v 14 Instead, put on the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} like clothing, and do not make plans to satisfy the desires of the flesh.
en.R: We should live in a way that is right for the daytime, when everyone can see. We should not go to wild parties or get drunk. We should not have sex outside of marriage or do shameful things. We should not fight or be jealous. \v 14 Instead, let the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} be like the clothes you wear. Do not keep thinking about how to give your sinful self what it wants.

es.L: Como en [el] día, andemos decentemente, no en orgías y borracheras, no en promiscuidad y desenfreno, no en contiendas y envidia, \v 14 sino {{plural_you:vístanse|vestíos}} del Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, y no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} provisión para la carne, para [sus] deseos.
es.B: Comportémonos con decencia, como la gente se comporta de día: no en fiestas desenfrenadas y borracheras, no en inmoralidad sexual y excesos desvergonzados, no en peleas y envidias. \v 14 Al contrario, {{plural_you:vístanse|vestíos}} del Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} como quien se pone la ropa, y no {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} planes para satisfacer los deseos de la carne.
es.R: Debemos vivir de un modo que convenga al día, cuando todos pueden ver. No vayamos a fiestas desenfrenadas ni nos emborrachemos. No tengamos relaciones sexuales fuera del matrimonio ni hagamos cosas vergonzosas. No peleemos ni tengamos envidia. \v 14 Al contrario, que el Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} sea como la ropa que {{plural_you:llevan|lleváis}} puesta. No {{plural_you:sigan|sigáis}} pensando en cómo darle a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} yo pecador lo que quiere.

sw.L: Kama katika mchana, na tutembee kwa heshima, si katika sherehe za anasa na ulevi, si katika uasherati na ufisadi, si katika ugomvi na wivu, \v 14 bali jivikeni Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, wala msiandae mpango kwa ajili ya mwili, kwa [ajili ya] tamaa [zake].
sw.B: Tuishi kwa adabu, kama watu waishivyo mchana: si katika sherehe za anasa na ulevi, si katika uasherati na tabia za aibu zisizo na kiasi, si katika ugomvi na wivu. \v 14 Badala yake, jivikeni Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kama vazi, wala msifanye mipango ya kutimiza tamaa za asili ya dhambi.
sw.R: Tunapaswa kuishi kwa namna inayofaa mchana, wakati kila mtu anaweza kuona. Tusiende kwenye sherehe za anasa wala kulewa. Tusifanye mapenzi nje ya ndoa wala kufanya mambo ya aibu. Tusigombane wala kuoneana wivu. \v 14 Badala yake, Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} awe kama nguo mnazovaa. Msiendelee kufikiria jinsi ya kuipa asili yenu ya dhambi kile inachotaka.

decisions.reason: κώμοις were drunken parties and night processions through the streets; κοίταις is literally "beds", sexual immorality; ἀσελγείαις is shameless indecency that no longer cares who sees. The last pair, strife and jealousy, shows that quarrels belong to the darkness as much as drunkenness.

alternatives: live as people who belong to the coming day
decisions.reason: περιπατήσωμεν ("walk") is the usual biblical word for how a person lives. "As in the day" means behaving as people do in daylight, where nothing is hidden; it also fits Paul's picture of the coming day (verse 12), so both may be meant.

decisions.choice: put on the Lord Jesus Christ: take on his life and character as one's own
decisions.reason: The clothing picture of verse 12 now has a person as the clothing. In Galatians 3:27 believers "have put on Christ" when baptized; here those who already belong to him are told to live out that union day by day.

decisions.choice: the sinful self opposed to God
decisions.reason: σαρκὸς here is human life turned against God, with desires of its own, as in Galatians 5:16-17. Paul does not mean the body as such.
πρόνοιαν is forethought: Paul forbids thinking ahead about how to satisfy those desires.
Readable says what "flesh" means here (m4), as in Galatians 5.

decisions.choice: have sex outside of marriage or do shameful things
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for what the two Greek words describe (m1).
Readable explains what living as in the daytime means (m2).

decisions.choice: like clothing / be like the clothes you wear
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the clothing picture clear (m3), since "put on" a person is not ordinary English.

"Mwili" is the body, and "tamaa za mwili" would sound like bodily appetites only. Here the word means the sinful self opposed to God (m4), so Balanced and Readable say "asili ya dhambi" (sinful nature). Literal keeps "mwili".
